topic: Discovery stories / peptides your body makes: leptin, the hormone your fat makes. 1950 the obese (ob) mouse appeared at the Jackson Laboratory, Maine (Lasker Foundation 2010); Douglas Coleman's parabiosis experiments: ob mouse joined to another mouse ate less, so ob mice lack a circulating hormone (Neill, JCI 2010); 1994 Friedman lab at Rockefeller cloned the ob gene, active in fat; named leptin from Greek leptos 'thin' (Zhang et al., Nature 1994; Lasker 2010); mature leptin 146 amino acids, made by white adipose tissue, blood level proportional to fat mass, acts on hypothalamus and brainstem, falling leptin = starvation signal (StatPearls 'Physiology, Leptin' 2023); 2010 Lasker Basic Medical Research Award to Coleman and Friedman

cards.html:
Discovery story

Your fat sends messages to your brain.

Maine, USA

1950

A very hungry mouse appears in a lab.

Named the ob mouse.

The experiment

Coleman joins two mice so they share blood.

The ob mouse eats less.

Normal blood has a signal it lacks.

New York

1994

Friedman finds the gene. It works in fat.

He names it leptin. Greek leptos = thin.

How it works

146

amino acids. More fat, more leptin.

Leptin falls? The brain reads starvation.

Save this for your physiology exam.
